extracted.subtask_description: A concise statement of ethical principles and professional standards for newspaper journalism, guiding reporters and editors on responsibilities such as accuracy, independence, impartiality, fairness, and defense of press freedom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preamble / Integrity obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: The First Amendment, protecting freedom of expression from abridgment by any law, guarantees to the people through their press a constitutional right, and thereby places on newspaper people a particular responsibility. Thus journalism demands of its practitioners not only industry and knowledge but also the pursuit of a standard of integrity proportionate to the journalist's singular obligation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets the overall purpose: the Statement of Principles is a standard encouraging the highest ethical and professional performance. Journalists must match the privilege of press freedom with a high standard of integrity and responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article I - Responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The primary purpose of gathering and distributing news and opinion is to serve the general welfare by informing the people and enabling them to make judgments on the issues of the time. Newspapermen and women who abuse the power of their professional role for selfish motives or unworthy purposes are faithless to that public trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists must serve the public welfare, inform citizens, enable civic judgment, and exercise independent scrutiny of powerful forces (including government). Avoid abusing professional power for selfish or unworthy purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article II - Freedom of the Press
rubrics_metrics.description: Freedom of the press belongs to the people. It must be defended against encroachment or assault from any quarter, public or private. Journalists must be constantly alert to see that the public's business is conducted in public. They must be vigilant against all who would exploit the press for selfish purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actively defend press freedom from all threats; monitor transparency of public institutions; resist uses of the press that serve private/selfish interests rather than the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article III - Independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists must avoid impropriety and the appearance of impropriety as well as any conflict of interest or the appearance of conflict. They should neither accept anything nor pursue any activity that might compromise or seem to compromise their integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid both actual conflicts of interest and appearances of conflict. Do not accept gifts/benefits or undertake activities that could compromise perceived integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article IV - Truth and Accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Good faith with the reader is the foundation of good journalism. Every effort must be made to assure that the news content is accurate, free from bias and in context, and that all sides are presented fairly. Editorials, analytical articles and commentary should be held to the same standards of accuracy with respect to facts as news reports. Significant errors of fact, as well as errors of omission, should be corrected promptly and prominently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make every effort to ensure factual accuracy, context, and freedom from bias; present all sides fairly; hold opinion/analysis to the same factual standards as news; correct significant factual errors and omissions quickly and prominently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article V - Impartiality
rubrics_metrics.description: To be impartial does not require the press to be unquestioning or to refrain from editorial expression. Sound practice, however, demands a clear distinction for the reader between news reports and opinion. Articles that contain opinion or personal interpretation should be clearly identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a clear separation between news and opinion; label opinion or interpretive pieces clearly so readers can distinguish editorial expression from news reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article VI - Fair Play
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists should respect the rights of people involved in the news, observe the common standards of decency and stand accountable to the public for the fairness and accuracy of their news reports. Persons publicly accused should be given the earliest opportunity to respond. Pledges of confidentiality to news sources must be honored at all costs, and therefore should not be given lightly. Unless there is clear and pressing need to maintain confidences, sources of information should be identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect subjects' rights and decency, provide accused persons an early chance to respond, honor confidentiality promises (but grant them cautiously), and identify sources except when there is a clear, pressing need for anonymity.
